description: We are Nexora, a team of passionate STEM High School students from Egypt with strong experience in scientific research, software development, programming, and engineering. We have participated in STEM competitions and developed innovative projects, strengthening our teamwork, creativity, and problem-solving skills. Through NASA Space Apps, we aim to turn ideas into impactful solutions. We welcome motivated members skilled in AI, coding, UI/UX, data science, and space exploration.
summary:
NOT JUST A DOT — Every Object Has a Story.

Inspired by the idea “I Am Not a Number,” NOT JUST A DOT was created to give every celestial object an identity beyond being just a dot on a map.

We developed an interactive web platform using real NASA SPHEREx Data Release 1 data, focusing on a carefully selected region of the actual sky. At its core is a real astronomical map of our selected region, where every plotted object represents a data point from the dataset.

When users click on an object, they unlock its story through an interactive profile featuring its astronomical image, coordinates, spectral fingerprint, scientific properties, historical context, and an interactive 3D visualization. We also introduce mathematical sonification, transforming spectral data into sound and adding an immersive dimension to the exploration experience.

Our project addresses the challenge of making complex astronomical data accessible and engaging. Rather than seeing countless points as anonymous data, users can explore the science behind each one.

Because the universe is more than numbers, and every dot has a story worth discovering.
details:
NOT JUST A DOT

Inspired by the idea “I Am Not a Number,” NOT JUST A DOT transforms astronomical data points into individual stories waiting to be discovered.

Our project is an interactive web platform built around real observations from NASA SPHEREx Data Release 1. Instead of displaying a generic representation of the universe, we work with a real astronomical map of a carefully selected region from the SPHEREx dataset. Each plotted object links to its corresponding data, letting users explore the objects in that region.

How does it work?

Users begin by exploring the selected sky region through an interactive map. When they click on an object, its profile reveals multiple layers of information:

- Astronomical Image: A visual representation of the selected object based on available astronomical observations.

- Cosmic Identity: Its coordinates, source information, and available observational context.

- Spectral Fingerprint: A visualization of its spectral measurements, helping users explore how it behaves across different infrared wavelengths.

- Interactive 3D Visualization: A new perspective that makes exploring celestial objects more engaging, while distinguishing illustrative visualizations from actual physical reconstructions.

- Cosmic Sound: A mathematical sonification experience that translates spectral measurements into sound through a defined mapping, allowing users to experience astronomical data in an entirely different way.

Benefits and Intended Impact

NOT JUST A DOT makes complex astronomical datasets easier to explore and understand. It connects scientific information with visual exploration and sound, helping students, educators, astronomy enthusiasts, and curious users engage with real space observations.

Our intended impact is to make scientific data feel less distant and more human-accessible, inspire curiosity about the universe, and encourage people to explore the science behind astronomical discoveries.

Tools and Technologies

We used NASA SPHEREx Data Release 1 as our primary scientific data source and Manus as an AI-assisted development platform to build the interactive web experience. The project combines web development, astronomical data processing, scientific visualization, interactive 3D graphics, and mathematical sonification.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The creative idea behind our project is simple: every dot has a story. We wanted to move beyond conventional astronomical maps and create an experience in which users do not simply look at objects but interact with their identities and scientific information.

Throughout development, we considered scientific accuracy, data authenticity, accessibility, user experience, and transparency. We aimed to make the experience visually engaging without presenting illustrative visualizations or mathematical sonification as direct physical observations.

NOT JUST A DOT Because every object in the universe deserves to be more than just a point on a map.
